The first is the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system I work on through Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus. I own major pieces of the data and ML infrastructure: the repository and CI scaffold, the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI microservice, and the public detection API. The modeling is temporal sequence modeling over event streams using RNN and Transformer-style approaches, with anomaly scoring and a learning-to-rank layer on top. I added the ranking layer because a detector that fires constantly just moves the problem onto the operator, so I also built a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so an analyst can see why something was flagged. That concern with operational usefulness and failure modes is what I would bring to autonomy software, where a wrong output has consequences.

The second is jobright-application-agent, a Playwright agent in TypeScript I built deliberately as a deterministic, operator-controlled system. Every application moves through an explicit state machine, SQLite is the single source of truth so state cannot diverge across processes, and every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed flags that never default on. I also built a validation ladder from unit to fixture to live read-only to live mutation, because a capability should not count as working until it has been tested against the level of reality it claims. I care about where automation should stop, not only where it can go.
